plan.hypothesis: Test whether R-squared differs from zero (all regression coefficients equal zero)
assumptions: Fixed linear regression model with intercept and 3 predictors
Null hypothesis: all regression coefficients (excluding intercept) equal zero
Test statistic follows noncentral F-distribution under the alternative
Anticipated multiple correlation ρ = 0.30 is fixed and known
Significance level α = 0.05, two-sided test
Denominator degrees of freedom = n - p = 80 - 4 = 76
Numerator degrees of freedom = p - 1 = 3
scientific_notes: The test is the omnibus F-test: F = [R²/(p-1)] / [(1-R²)/(n-p)] where R² = (multiple correlation)²
Noncentrality parameter λ = R² * (n - p) / (1 - R²)
Power derived from P(F_{p-1, n-p, λ} > F_{crit})
Standard approach for testing overall model significance in linear regression

assumptions: Fixed linear regression model with intercept and 3 predictors (p = 4 parameters total)

limitations: Power calculation assumes fixed anticipated correlation; actual power will vary if observed correlation differs
The model assumes standard linear regression assumptions (linearity, normality, homoscedasticity, independence)
Power is moderate (59.9%) with the given parameters; larger sample size or effect size would increase power
Calculation does not account for predictor collinearity or other model specification issues

# Linear regression power calculation for testing R-squared against zero
# Using noncentral F-distribution

# Parameters
rho <- 0.30                           # Multiple correlation coefficient
R2 <- rho^2                            # Coefficient of determination
n <- 80                                # Sample size (participants)
p <- 4                                 # Number of parameters (intercept + 3 predictors)
alpha <- 0.05                          # Significance level
df_numerator <- p - 1                  # Degrees of freedom numerator = 3
df_denominator <- n - p                # Degrees of freedom denominator = 76

# Critical F-value at alpha = 0.05
F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df_numerator, df_denominator)

# Noncentrality parameter
# lambda = F-statistic under the alternative hypothesis
# F = [R^2 / (p-1)] / [(1-R^2) / (n-p)]
# lambda = R^2 * (n - p) / (1 - R^2)
lambda <- R2 * df_denominator / (1 - R2)

# Power = P(F > F_crit) under noncentrality lambda
power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df_numerator, df_denominator, ncp = lambda)

# Create results object
results <- data.frame(
  metric = c("power", "multiple_correlation", "sample_size", "R_squared", 
             "df_numerator", "df_denominator", "noncentrality_parameter", 
             "critical_F_value", "alpha"),
  value = c(power, rho, n, R2, df_numerator, df_denominator, lambda, F_crit, alpha),
  unit = c("probability", "correlation", "participants", "proportion", 
           "degrees_of_freedom", "degrees_of_freedom", "noncentrality", 
           "F_statistic", "significance_level")
)

print(results)

# Format output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
output_results <- list(
  list(metric = "power", value = round(power, 15), unit = "probability")
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = output_results), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Correct noncentrality parameter definition
# For testing R^2 = 0, the noncentral F follows F(p-1, n-p, lambda) where:
# lambda is the NONCENTRALITY parameter, NOT the F-statistic scaled by df

rho <- 0.30
R2 <- rho^2
n <- 80
p <- 4
alpha <- 0.05

df_num <- p - 1  # = 3
df_den <- n - p  # = 76

# The noncentrality parameter for noncentral F is defined as:
# lambda = (population effect) * sqrt(df_den / df_num)
# OR equivalently, if F_expected is the expected F-statistic under HA:
# The R function pf and qf use the relationship:
# E[F(df1, df2, lambda)] relates to lambda directly

# For regression R^2 test:
# The noncentrality is typically lambda = [rho^2 / (1 - rho^2)] * (n - p)
# This is because under HA, E[MSR] / E[MSE] gives an offset F-statistic

# Using the standard formula for noncentrality in F-test of regression:
lambda <- (R2 / (1 - R2)) * df_den

# Critical F-value
F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df_num, df_den)

# Power = P(F > F_crit) where F ~ F(df_num, df_den, lambda)
power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df_num, df_den, ncp = lambda)

cat("=== CORRECT NONCENTRALITY PARAMETER ===\n")
cat(sprintf("R-squared (effect size): %.4f\n", R2))
cat(sprintf("Sample size: %d\n", n))
cat(sprintf("Parameters (including intercept): %d\n", p))
cat(sprintf("Numerator df: %d\n", df_num))
cat(sprintf("Denominator df: %d\n", df_den))
cat("\nNoncentrality formula: lambda = [R²/(1-R²)] * (n-p)\n")
cat(sprintf("lambda = [%.4f / %.4f] * %d\n", R2, 1-R2, df_den))
cat(sprintf("lambda = %.6f\n", lambda))
cat("\nCritical F-value: %.6f\n", F_crit)
cat(sprintf("Power = P(F > %.6f) = %.6f\n", F_crit, power))

# Output for submission
results <- list(
  list(metric = "power", value = round(power, 15), unit = "probability")
)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = results), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Evidence e1; success=true

# Linear regression power calculation for testing R-squared against zero
# Using noncentral F-distribution

# Parameters
rho <- 0.30                           # Multiple correlation coefficient
R2 <- rho^2                            # Coefficient of determination
n <- 80                                # Sample size (participants)
p <- 4                                 # Number of parameters (intercept + 3 predictors)
alpha <- 0.05                          # Significance level
df_numerator <- p - 1                  # Degrees of freedom numerator = 3
df_denominator <- n - p                # Degrees of freedom denominator = 76

# Critical F-value at alpha = 0.05
F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df_numerator, df_denominator)

# Noncentrality parameter
# lambda = F-statistic under the alternative hypothesis
# F = [R^2 / (p-1)] / [(1-R^2) / (n-p)]
# lambda = R^2 * (n - p) / (1 - R^2)
lambda <- R2 * df_denominator / (1 - R2)

# Power = P(F > F_crit) under noncentrality lambda
power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df_numerator, df_denominator, ncp = lambda)

# Create results object
results <- data.frame(
  metric = c("power", "multiple_correlation", "sample_size", "R_squared", 
             "df_numerator", "df_denominator", "noncentrality_parameter", 
             "critical_F_value", "alpha"),
  value = c(power, rho, n, R2, df_numerator, df_denominator, lambda, F_crit, alpha),
  unit = c("probability", "correlation", "participants", "proportion", 
           "degrees_of_freedom", "degrees_of_freedom", "noncentrality", 
           "F_statistic", "significance_level")
)

print(results)

# Format output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
output_results <- list(
  list(metric = "power", value = round(power, 15), unit = "probability")
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = output_results), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))


# Evidence e2; success=true

# Verification of the power calculation

rho <- 0.30
R2 <- rho^2
n <- 80
p <- 4
alpha <- 0.05

df_num <- p - 1
df_den <- n - p

# Step 1: Verify R-squared value
print(paste("Multiple correlation (rho):", rho))
print(paste("R-squared (rho^2):", R2))

# Step 2: Verify degrees of freedom
print(paste("Numerator df (p-1):", df_num))
print(paste("Denominator df (n-p):", df_den))

# Step 3: Critical F-value
F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df_num, df_den)
print(paste("Critical F-value at alpha=0.05:", round(F_crit, 6)))

# Step 4: Noncentrality parameter
# Under HA: lambda = F * df_den where F is the expected F-statistic
# F = [R^2 / (p-1)] / [(1-R^2) / (n-p)]
# Simplifying: lambda = R^2 * (n-p) / (1-R^2)
lambda <- R2 * df_den / (1 - R2)
print(paste("Noncentrality parameter (lambda):", round(lambda, 6)))

# Alternative expression for verification:
# Using the formula F_expected = [R^2 / (p-1)] / [(1-R^2) / (n-p)]
F_expected <- (R2 / df_num) / ((1 - R2) / df_den)
lambda_alt <- F_expected * df_den / df_num
print(paste("Lambda (alternative formula):", round(lambda_alt, 6)))

# Step 5: Power = P(F(df_num, df_den, lambda) > F_crit)
power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df_num, df_den, ncp = lambda)
print(paste("Power (1 - CDF at F_crit):", round(power, 6)))

# Visualize the distribution
x_vals <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 500)
pdf_central <- df(x_vals, df_num, df_den, ncp = 0)
pdf_noncentral <- df(x_vals, df_num, df_den, ncp = lambda)

cat("\n--- Summary ---\n")
cat("Test: Omnibus F-test for R-squared = 0 in linear regression\n")
cat("H0: All regression coefficients (except intercept) = 0\n")
cat("H1: At least one regression coefficient ≠ 0\n")
cat("Test statistic: F = [R²/(p-1)] / [(1-R²)/(n-p)]\n")
cat(sprintf("Achieved power at n=%d: %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", n, power, 100*power))


# Evidence e3; success=true

# Correct noncentrality parameter definition
# For testing R^2 = 0, the noncentral F follows F(p-1, n-p, lambda) where:
# lambda is the NONCENTRALITY parameter, NOT the F-statistic scaled by df

rho <- 0.30
R2 <- rho^2
n <- 80
p <- 4
alpha <- 0.05

df_num <- p - 1  # = 3
df_den <- n - p  # = 76

# The noncentrality parameter for noncentral F is defined as:
# lambda = (population effect) * sqrt(df_den / df_num)
# OR equivalently, if F_expected is the expected F-statistic under HA:
# The R function pf and qf use the relationship:
# E[F(df1, df2, lambda)] relates to lambda directly

# For regression R^2 test:
# The noncentrality is typically lambda = [rho^2 / (1 - rho^2)] * (n - p)
# This is because under HA, E[MSR] / E[MSE] gives an offset F-statistic

# Using the standard formula for noncentrality in F-test of regression:
lambda <- (R2 / (1 - R2)) * df_den

# Critical F-value
F_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df_num, df_den)

# Power = P(F > F_crit) where F ~ F(df_num, df_den, lambda)
power <- 1 - pf(F_crit, df_num, df_den, ncp = lambda)

cat("=== CORRECT NONCENTRALITY PARAMETER ===\n")
cat(sprintf("R-squared (effect size): %.4f\n", R2))
cat(sprintf("Sample size: %d\n", n))
cat(sprintf("Parameters (including intercept): %d\n", p))
cat(sprintf("Numerator df: %d\n", df_num))
cat(sprintf("Denominator df: %d\n", df_den))
cat("\nNoncentrality formula: lambda = [R²/(1-R²)] * (n-p)\n")
cat(sprintf("lambda = [%.4f / %.4f] * %d\n", R2, 1-R2, df_den))
cat(sprintf("lambda = %.6f\n", lambda))
cat("\nCritical F-value: %.6f\n", F_crit)
cat(sprintf("Power = P(F > %.6f) = %.6f\n", F_crit, power))

# Output for submission
results <- list(
  list(metric = "power", value = round(power, 15), unit = "probability")
)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = results), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
